**Ch 073 draft — scan**

The chapter is clean. The authorized digression removal (Ahab's Sphynx address) is actually retained in the draft almost in full. All pronouns have clear antecedents, the dialogue exchange is complete, and no mid-scene jump occurs.

**Ch 074 draft — scan**

**Candidate 1:** "As the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of a sperm whale already hoisted alongside, many strange things were hinted in reference to this wild affair."

The source reads: "As, after this interlude, the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale…" — referring to the same Pequod whale whose head was hoisted in Ch 073. The draft changes this to "a sperm whale already hoisted alongside," which is consistent with what the draft established in Ch 073. No structural damage here — a reader can follow this.

**Candidate 2:** "Stubb alluded to a strange story told of the Jeroboam and this very man, who had gained a wonderful ascendency over almost everybody in her crew."

The source explains that Stubb's knowledge came from the Town-Ho gam, which is an authorized subplot removal (the Town-Ho gam is not on the authorized removal list, but the sentence in the draft does mention "the Town-Ho's company told us of" in Stubb's exclamation immediately before, so the antecedent "this very man" is clear). No structural damage.

**Candidate 3:** "As he studied it, Starbuck took a cutting-spade pole, slightly split the end, and so handed the letter across without the boat coming closer."

Source: "As he was studying it out, Starbuck took a long cutting-spade pole, and with his knife slightly split the end, to insert the letter there, and in that way, hand it to the boat, without its coming any closer to the ship." The draft compression omits the insertion of the letter into the split end of the pole. This matters because the next paragraph has Ahab "caught it in the slit of the pole" — the draft does mention "the slit of the pole" later, and the reader can piece together that the pole-slit was used to hold the letter. Not a structural failure — slightly less ornamented but parseable.

**Candidate 4 — the one genuine structural issue:**

"But as the side-ladder was being rigged, the stranger waved his hand in token that this was unnecessary."

The source reads: "as the side-ladder was being rigged by Starbuck's order to accommodate the visiting captain, the stranger in question waved his hand from his boat's stern." The draft cuts "the stranger in question" and just writes "the stranger" — but more importantly, the pronoun "the stranger" here must refer to the captain of the Jeroboam, but the immediately preceding sentence names no individual captain; it says "she ranged abeam… and lowered a boat." The name "Captain Mayhew" has not yet appeared in the draft at this point; it comes only after this sentence. So "the stranger" is ambiguous — it could be a crewman in the boat. However, a competent reader will infer that the captain of the lowered boat waved off the ladder — this is conventional enough that it's not genuine confusion.

**Candidate 5 — genuine structural damage:**

"'I tell thee again, Gabriel, that—' But again the boat tore ahead as if dragged by fiends."

In the source, Ahab says "I tell thee again, Gabriel, that—" which references something previously said. In the source, Ahab had first said "I fear not thy epidemic, man… come on board" and then the interrupted exchange establishes repetition. In the draft this is preserved. No problem here.

**Candidate 6:**

"Meantime, Gabriel from the mast-head was tossing one arm in frantic gestures, hurling forth prophecies of speedy doom."

Source: "Gabriel, ascending to the main-royal mast-head, was tossing one arm in frantic gestures, and hurling forth prophecies of speedy doom to the sacrilegious assailants of his divinity."

The draft omits "ascending to" — Gabriel is simply placed at the mast-head with no transition. But the reader understands Gabriel went up there. Not structural damage.

**Candidate 7 — Macey:**

"But when, a year or two afterwards, Moby Dick was sighted from the mast-heads, Macey, the chief mate, burned with ardour to encounter him"

The name "Macey" appears here with the gloss "the chief mate" — sufficient. Later: "the luckless mate, so full of furious life, was smitten bodily into the air" — no name, just "the mate," clear antecedent. Then: "Ahab muttered, '…Mr. Harry Macey, Ship Jeroboam;—why it's Macey, and he's dead!'" — this is a direct quotation identifying Macey, so fine.

After careful review, I find **no valid structural coherence failures** in either draft that meet the gate test. The compression is consistently clean at the structural level.
